title: Verify #331 removeStaleFiles blast radius on the yacht (deploy path vs container-data path)
description: GATING CHECK for GH#331. removeStaleFiles (deploy.go:163,311) runs --delete semantics over each /mnt/appdata/<service> dir on every default-config reconcile (ContentHashSync default-on, shipped v0.12.0 Feb 2026). Repo appdata/<service> dirs are config-only, but authelia (db.sqlite3, users.yml), grafana (grafana.db), gatus (data/) store live runtime data in those same dirs per their compose mounts (/mnt/user/appdata/...). By code, this should have wiped authelia in Feb; it hasn't. Hypothesis: local_appdata_path=/mnt/appdata is DISTINCT storage from the containers' /mnt/user/appdata mounts, so removeStaleFiles operates on a delivery tree that doesn't hold live DBs. This is undocumented and load-bearing. Verify on the box: stat -c '%d:%i %n' /mnt/appdata/authelia/db.sqlite3 /mnt/user/appdata/authelia/db.sqlite3 — same device:inode => SAME storage => actively dangerous; different/missing => distinct => safe-by-accident. Also grep daemon logs for 'Removed stale' under authelia/grafana/gatus. Outcome decides whether GH#331 fix is P0-urgent or P2-convenient.
notes:
RESOLVED BY CODE ANALYSIS (2026-05-26). The path-split hypothesis is REFUTED — storage is SHARED, so #331 was genuinely dangerous, not safe-by-accident.

Topology (from homelab compose files):
- authelia (manifests/services/authelia.yml:26): host /mnt/user/appdata/authelia -> container /config; DB at /config/db.sqlite3 (configuration.yml.tmpl:53) => host /mnt/user/appdata/authelia/db.sqlite3
- bosun (unraid/appdata/bosun/docker-compose.yml:92): host /mnt/user/appdata -> container /mnt/appdata; local_appdata_path=/mnt/appdata => bosun's authelia deploy target = host /mnt/user/appdata/authelia (SAME dir)
- Repo source for authelia is config-only (only configuration.yml.tmpl tracked), so old removeStaleFiles compared config-only staging vs a target holding db.sqlite3/users.yml and would delete them.

NOTE: the original on-box 'stat /mnt/appdata/... /mnt/user/appdata/...' check is misleading — /mnt/appdata is a CONTAINER-ONLY path (bind mount), so it does not exist on the Unraid host; stat would report ENOENT, not 'distinct storage'. The equivalence is definitional via the bind mount.

Why data survived despite the bug (not yet confirmed, secondary): likely SQLite auto-recreates db.sqlite3 on authelia restart (post-sync hook restarts authelia), masking loss as session resets rather than an outage; OR the content-hash stale-removal path was not firing as assumed. ONLY remaining on-box check worth running: grep bosun daemon logs for 'Removed stale' under authelia/grafana/gatus to confirm whether the old prune was actually executing.

Fix shipped in PR #366 (managed-set prune) — correct and was addressing real shared storage.
close_reason: Answered by code analysis (recorded in notes): storage is SHARED, not split — bosun's /mnt/appdata is a bind mount of host /mnt/user/appdata, the same dir authelia/grafana/gatus write runtime data to. #331 was genuinely dangerous. Managed-set fix shipped + merged in PR #366. Optional log-grep forensic (was the old prune firing) does not change the fix; not gating.

title: Deploy invariant false-fails on no-op content-hash sync (GH#330)
description: verifyDeployTarget fires ErrDeployInvariantEmptyWrite when content-hash sync writes 0 files against a non-empty source. Fix: in the empty-writes branch, inspect the destination — pass if every source file exists at dst (existence only, no mtime check), keep erroring only when files are genuinely missing. title: Fix #333 partial compose failure reported as success
description: GH#333. ComposeUpIsolated (internal/reconcile/compose.go:376-380) returns nil unless ALL compose files fail; a 1-of-N failure returns success. Caller (reconcile.go:628-630,670) then fires a success alert, sets LastDeployedCommit, clears NeedsRedeploy -> the failed stack never retries and no alert fires. Default critical path for any multi-stack deploy (homelab runs many). Fix: treat any per-file compose failure as a deploy failure (or surface partial-failure state that keeps NeedsRedeploy set and alerts). Same 'success before proven' root class as GH#330.
close_reason: Fixed in 9f2a1c1 (PR #363): partial compose failure now returns an error from deployLocal instead of falling through to success. New partialDeployError() pure helper in pure.go + TestPartialDeployError (4 cases). Mirrors the health-gate's treat-as-failure behavior. Behavior change: partial deploys now report failure + retry instead of silent success.

title: Fix #331 removeStaleFiles: add protect-list + Lstat + empty-source guard
description: GH#331. removeStaleFiles (internal/reconcile/deploy.go:268-337) has no protect-list, follows symlinks via os.Stat (vs CopyDirIfChanged's Lstat-skip), and on an empty/symlink-only source would RemoveAll the entire target. Even where today's path split protects live data, the safety is incidental. Fix: (1) skip-delete a configurable protect-list of runtime artifacts (*.sqlite3, *.db, data/, etc.) or invert to an explicit managed-files set; (2) Lstat semantics to match the sync side; (3) refuse to mirror-delete when the source resolved empty (guard against a render producing 0 files wiping the target). Mirror verify_test.go patterns. Blocked by the on-box verification which determines urgency and whether a protect-list or a managed-set redesign is warranted.
close_reason: Fixed in fix/deploy-chain-hardening-331-332: #331 managed-set prune, #332/#335 rollback archive extraction

title: Fix deploy invariant false-fail on no-op content-hash sync (GH#330)
description:
GH#330: verifyDeployTarget treats a legitimate no-op content-hash sync (0 writes, dst already byte-matches src) as corruption (ErrDeployInvariantEmptyWrite), aborting the entire reconcile before compose-up. Caused a 62-container homelab outage (0/1 targets succeeded). Latent bug exposed by the #319 backup-bounding fix.

Root redesign: verify on-disk truth (files present + content-equal via fileutil.FileHash/ContentEqual) instead of the write counter. Also fixes two siblings in the same PR: standard-mode (CONTENT_HASH_SYNC=false) never records writes -> invariant aborts every non-empty target; single-file symlink target -> silent no-op then invariant abort.

Files: internal/reconcile/verify.go (zero-write branch + dirHasRegularFiles Lstat), internal/reconcile/deploy.go (DeployLocalFile ErrSymlinkSkipped swallow). Tests mirror internal/reconcile/verify_test.go.
close_reason: Fixed via 665ac04 (verify.go on-disk-truth redesign + deploy.go ErrSymlinkSkipped swallow), bf7ef1a (filed 31 sibling issues GH#331-361), cb0ff13 (locking diagram + LR->TD shrink), 2c5292f (doc freshness + skill mirror). 11 regression tests pass; full suite green except one Docker-gated subtest (colima down, environmental). Also resolves B1 standard-mode + B2 single-file-symlink siblings.

title: Reconcile #312 backup-failure semantics vs shipped #319 (spec conflict)
description:
PR #312 (spec/add-backup-integrity-semantics, bosun-8s5) MODIFIES the same 'Configuration Backup' requirement that #319/#324 just shipped + archived (canonical openspec/specs/reconcile/spec.md as of e0748aa / archive 2026-05-25-add-backup-deadline-and-self-exclusion).

OpenSpec MODIFIED blocks REPLACE the whole requirement on archive. #312's delta is a full rewrite that does NOT carry #319's clauses and CONTRADICTS one:

- #319 (canonical now): 'Backup failures, including timeouts, SHALL log a warning but SHALL NOT abort the deployment pipeline.' Plus self-exclusion invariant + BackupTimeout (5m, BOSUN_BACKUP_TIMEOUT).
- #312 (proposed): 'When a required backup cannot be created or verified, the reconciler SHALL abort the reconcile before mutating target state.' (fail-closed)

FOOTGUN: archiving #312 as-is would (1) silently drop the self-exclusion + BackupTimeout clauses, and (2) flip backup-failure from best-effort to fail-closed.

RESOLUTION NEEDED before #312 reaches ready-to-build: #312's MODIFIED block must become a true superset that also states self-exclusion + BackupTimeout, and the abort-vs-continue tension must be resolved explicitly. Candidate framings: (A) fail-closed wins, incl. timeout=abort (bounded+gated); (B) carve-out: verification/corruption=abort, timeout/self-exclusion-miss=warn+continue (preserves #319's 'a hang must never block'); (C) #312 narrows abort to genuine corruption only. Decision is the author's product call.
close_reason: Resolved via framing (A) fail-closed, bounded by #319's timeout. #312's spec delta (pushed 034a8c2) now re-states #319's three clauses verbatim (BackupTimeout/BOSUN_BACKUP_TIMEOUT, ctx-bound verification, self-exclusion invariant) so archive cannot revert them, and adds a MODIFIED Pipeline Orchestration requirement flipping the stage-7 carve-out to: nothing-to-back-up proceeds, required-backup failure (incl. timeout) aborts before state mutation. openspec validate --strict passes. The merge-ordering footgun is closed.

title: Tier-1 wedge-class fixes: emergency runComposeUp ctx + webhook body cap
description:

2. internal/cmd/webhook.go: 5 handlers (lines 171/215/285/348/413) read request bodies with raw io.ReadAll(r.Body), NO cap, while daemon/server.go caps every handler at maxWebhookBodySize=1MB. The standalone receiver is tunnel-exposed (GitLab/Gitea/Bitbucket) -> internet-facing DoS. Wrap in io.LimitReader(maxWebhookBodySize) + set Server.MaxHeaderBytes.

title: Fix #319: pre-deploy backup wedges reconcile (recursion + no timeout)
description:
GH#319. Cold/empty-state reconcile hangs forever in the pre-deploy backup step; nothing downstream deploys.

Three root causes (all confirmed in code):
1. Recursive self-inclusion: backupPathsFromTargets (reconcile.go:1125) includes /mnt/appdata/bosun (bosun is a deploy target); tar output lives at BackupDir (/app/backups -> host /mnt/appdata/bosun/backups) INSIDE a backed-up path, and tar (backup.go:89) has no --exclude, so it archives its own growing output (observed 8GB+).
2. VerifyBackup (backup.go:37) uses plain exec.Command('tar','-tzf',...) not CommandContext -> no caller deadline can kill it.
3. createBackup is the only Run() pipeline step not wrapped in context.WithTimeout (git/ssh/compose all are).

Fix (minimal, non-colliding with spec PR #312):
- backup.go: add --exclude for backup destination in Backup() and BackupRemote().
- backup.go: VerifyBackup(ctx, ...) using exec.CommandContext.
- reconcile.go/config: BackupTimeout + BOSUN_BACKUP_TIMEOUT, wrap createBackup ctx; on timeout warn+continue (spec line 217 already non-fatal).

Bundled Tier-1 siblings (NOT spec-coupled):
- emergency.go:730 runComposeUp: thread ctx + CommandContext + timeout (recovery path must not hang).
- cmd/webhook.go (5 handlers, lines 171/215/285/348/413): wrap io.ReadAll(r.Body) in io.LimitReader(maxWebhookBodySize=1MB) + set Server.MaxHeaderBytes (tunnel-exposed DoS asymmetry vs daemon/server.go).

Requires separate OpenSpec change proposal (Configuration Backup: bounded deadline + self-exclusion invariant), merge-ordered vs PR #312. Plan: ~/.claude/plans/what-s-up-big-dog-toasty-porcupine.md
notes: IMPLEMENTED: PR #324 open (fix/backup-deadline-and-self-exclusion), 4 commits = spec task groups 1-3+5. Group 4 (emergency/webhook) shipped via #321. Self-exclusion --exclude in Backup+BackupRemote; VerifyBackup(ctx) + 6 callers; Config.BackupTimeout + BOSUN_BACKUP_TIMEOUT (daemon env parse) + createBackup ctx wrap. Tests: TestBackup_ExcludesBackupDestination, TestVerifyBackup_HonorsCancelledContext, TestCreateBackup_HonorsBackupTimeout, TestConfigFromEnv_BackupTimeout all green. openspec validate strict = valid. Pending: CodeRabbit review on #324, then merge + archive openspec change + coordinate spec delta with #312 (whichever merges 2nd rebases). Keep in_progress until #324 merges.
close_reason: PR #324 squash-merged to main (e0748aa). All 5 spec task groups done; CodeRabbit approved (6 threads resolved); polish pass applied. Self-exclusion + ctx-aware verify + BackupTimeout shipped.

title: Fix local-deploy sync silent no-op (GH #214)
description: Local-deploy mode reports success while rendered templates never overwrite /mnt/user/appdata/<path>. Compose-up exits 0 against stale on-disk file. Drift check warns but is suppressed. Only 1 of 7 expected post-sync hooks fires. Repro: push commit changing .tmpl content; host-side grep + mtime confirms no write occurred despite render success. See plan: ~/.claude/plans/harmonic-spinning-cocoa.md (to be copied to docs/plans/2026-05-17-fix-local-deploy-sync-invariant.md).
design: Three-layer fix: defensive invariants (independent value), diagnostic run (root cause confirmation), targeted fix. Spec-before-code per project discipline. Spec branch first, ready-to-build label gates implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Layer 1: declared_services=0 fails reconcile unless BOSUN_ALLOW_EMPTY_DECLARED_STATE=true. Per-file write log lines in CopyDirIfChanged. Post-deploy mtime invariant blocks compose-up when WrittenFiles empty against non-empty source. Layer 2: diagnostic run identifies root cause. Layer 3: targeted fix applied. Tests cover all invariants. OpenSpec proposal merged before implementation begins.
notes: LAYER 2 COMPLETE (root cause confirmed via static trace + ground-truth homelab config, no live diagnostic needed). ROOT CAUSE: BOSUN_INFRA_DIR="." in homelab unraid/appdata/bosun/docker-compose.yml:32, but infra is nested at unraid/. None of the 3 plan hypotheses exact — it's a 4th: InfraSubDir misconfiguration that's internally consistent across render/discover/deploy. With InfraSubDir='.', stagingSubDir=repo root: ExtractDeclaredState globs staging/compose (missing→ErrComposeDirMissing, fatal), discoverDeployTargets treats unraid/.beads/.claude as targets, deploy maps staging/unraid→appdata/unraid (so freshrss landed at appdata/unraid/compose/, operator grep'd stale appdata/compose/). discovery.go:25-31 docstring confirms infra-sub-dir MUST directly contain appdata/ and compose/. FIX: (A) homelab BOSUN_INFRA_DIR=unraid + drop unraid/ prefix from bosun.yaml hook globs; (B optional) bosun hardening: ErrComposeDirMissing should scan siblings and suggest BOSUN_INFRA_DIR=<found>. NOTE: v0.34.0 daemon now fails loud (ErrComposeDirMissing) every reconcile since deploy — homelab deploys blocked until config fixed.

title: Port internal/docker from docker/docker v28 to moby/moby/{api,client} split modules
description:
The Go SDK at github.com/docker/docker is end-of-line at v28.5.2+incompatible. Five open Dependabot CVEs (3 high, 2 medium) trace to that module path. Their patched versions live in the new split modules:

- github.com/moby/moby/api    v1.54.2 (latest, types/container/system)
- github.com/moby/moby/client v0.4.1  (latest, the Client and *Options)

Migration is structural, not a sed:

- All *Options types moved from api/types/container -> client package
  (ContainerListOptions, ContainerLogsOptions, ContainerStopOptions, etc.)
- Every method gained an options parameter:
  Ping(ctx) -> Ping(ctx, PingOptions{})
  Info(ctx) -> Info(ctx, InfoOptions{})
  DiskUsage(ctx, opts) -> DiskUsage(ctx, opts) -- now returns DiskUsageResult
- Return types are now *Result wrappers (ContainerListResult instead of []container.Summary)
- types.Ping / types.HijackedResponse moved or renamed

Surface to touch (17 files probed during PR #380 investigation):

- internal/docker/{client,containers,interface}.go
- internal/docker/dockertest/mock.go
- internal/docker/*_test.go (3)
- internal/reconcile/*_test.go (8 — mock_docker_test, drift_*, hooks, health*, restart_breaker, reconcile)
- internal/daemon/api_docker_test.go

The DockerAPI interface in internal/docker/interface.go is the contract — port it first, then the impl in client.go/containers.go, then the mocks, then the tests. Mechanical sed of import paths works cleanly (go mod tidy resolves), the API rewrite is the real cost.

Operationally: all 5 CVEs are daemon-side (race conditions in docker cp, AuthZ plugin bypass, etc.). Bosun is a client-only consumer; none are exploitable from our usage. The homelab re-enable gate is the Engine daemon version on Unraid, not the linked SDK. So this is hygiene work to clear the Dependabot dashboard, not a security-critical bump.

CVEs that close on completion:
- GHSA-rg2x-37c3-w2rh (high)  docker cp race -> bind mount redirect
- GHSA-x86f-5xw2-fm2r (high)  PUT /containers/{id}/archive RCE
- GHSA-x744-4wpc-v9h2 (high)  AuthZ plugin bypass via oversized body
- GHSA-vp62-88p7-qqf5 (med)   docker cp symlink swap
- GHSA-pxq6-2prw-chj9 (med)   off-by-one in plugin priv validation

Probe artifacts (kept for reference, can re-run):
- /Users/cameron/.claude/jobs/34a4eb57/tmp/probe-moby-split.sh
- /Users/cameron/.claude/jobs/34a4eb57/tmp/inspect-new-api.sh
- /Users/cameron/.claude/jobs/34a4eb57/tmp/inspect-client.sh
- /Users/cameron/.claude/jobs/34a4eb57/tmp/port-docker-imports.sh

Out of scope for the eventual port:

title: Cluster H: re-state stage-9 invariant in Pipeline Orchestration delta before archiving
description: LATENT FOOTGUN surfaced during bosun-1xr. title: Harden deploy invariant: content-equality + symlink semantics (salvage #362)
description: PR #368 (merged a567eaf) fixed GH#330 with an existence-only destination check (firstMissingSourceFile). PR #362 had a stronger version worth porting on top of main: replace existence-only with destinationSatisfiesSource — confirm each src regular file is content-EQUAL at dst (reuse fileutil.FileHash/ContentEqual, the same primitives CopyFileIfChanged uses, so 'skipped because equal' and 'verified present' share one definition). Also: dirHasRegularFiles Lstat semantics so a symlink-only source imposes no write requirement (B2), and DeployLocalFile standard mode should swallow the benign ErrSymlinkSkipped sentinel (matches content-hash mode + CopyDir). Source: #362 branch fix/deploy-invariant-330, internal/reconcile/verify.go + deploy.go + verify_test.go (content-equality, symlink, and B1 standard-mode tests).
notes: Implemented on fix/harden-deploy-invariant-lov; PR #371 open. verify.go: destinationSatisfiesSource (content-equality via fileutil.FileHash/ContentEqual) + fileEqual, dirHasRegularFiles->Lstat. deploy.go: DeployLocalFile standard mode swallows ErrSymlinkSkipped (B2). Tests: stale-content+symlink-only table cases, TestDestinationSatisfiesSource, B1 standard-mode pass, standard-mode symlink swallow. Spec Invariant 3 existence->content-equality + 2 new scenarios. Docs: gitops.md + troubleshooting.md (mismatch= field). Awaiting CodeRabbit review.

Hardened deploy invariant: existence->content-equality (destinationSatisfiesSource + fileEqual reusing fileutil.FileHash/ContentEqual), symlink Lstat semantics (dirHasRegularFiles), DeployLocalFile standard-mode ErrSymlinkSkipped swallow (B2). title: Fix #332/#335 hollow rollback recovery (backup tarball vs loose-file rollback)
description: GH#332 (+#335). title: spec-review CI validates wrong change ID for fold-style spec PRs
description: The Spec Review Gate workflow (.github/workflows/spec-review.yml) derives CHANGE_ID from the branch name via CHANGE_ID=${BRANCH#spec/}. This assumes branch name == change ID, which holds for net-new proposals but breaks for fold/refactor PRs. Example: PR #313 branch spec/fold-cluster-c-multitarget edits the existing change add-multi-target-reconcile, so CI runs 'openspec validate fold-cluster-c-multitarget --strict' -> 'Unknown item' -> Validate Spec FAILURE, even though 'openspec validate add-multi-target-reconcile --strict' passes locally. Fix: detect the changed change-dir(s) from the PR diff (git diff --name-only under openspec/changes/<id>/) and validate those, instead of inferring from branch name. Affects any fold-style spec PR.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #328 (merged 2026-05-25). Validate Spec now derives change IDs from the PR's base..HEAD diff under openspec/changes/<id>/ (validates each, multi-change safe), falls back to branch name for net-new proposals, and adds fetch-depth:0. actionlint clean; functionally verified against #313's fold paths and a real on-main change.

title: docker client: honor ctx in io drains + don't shadow caller deadline in Ping
description:
Sweep finding (Tier 3, sibling of #319/bosun-k88). internal/docker/client.go:
- :342 io.Copy(io.Discard, attachResp.Reader) and :410 io.Copy(io.Discard, stats.Body) drain output ignoring ctx cancellation -> can block forever on a stuck docker daemon.
- :386 io.ReadAll of logs is size-bounded (100MB) but ignores ctx deadline.
- :86 Ping() wraps context.WithTimeout(ctx, 5s) but does NOT inherit a tighter caller deadline (shadows instead of min).
Fix: enforce ctx deadlines on the drains (e.g. copy in a goroutine selected against ctx.Done, or set read deadlines) and make Ping respect a tighter parent deadline.

title: Reconcile pipeline: add per-step timeouts to decrypt/render/hooks
description:
Sweep finding (Tier 2, sibling of #319/bosun-k88). In reconcile.go Run(), only git/compose/health derive per-step deadlines via context.WithTimeout. These steps inherit an unbounded parent ctx and can hang the reconcile:
- decrypt secrets (reconcile.go:485) — SOPS could hang.
- render templates (reconcile.go:511) — template/file I/O.
- post-sync hooks (reconcile.go:633) — hook subprocess exec.
Fix: wrap each in context.WithTimeout mirroring composeUpTimeout()/git timeouts; make durations configurable via BOSUN_* env where sensible.

title: Fix Validate Spec CI workflow: openspec-cli npm package does not exist

The actual openspec v1.2.0 tool used locally comes from Homebrew. Result: every spec PR's Validate Spec check fails with npm 404. First observed on PR #227. Fix options: install from a different source (Go install, curl release tarball, brew, etc.), publish openspec to npm properly, or remove the npm install step and use a different distribution mechanism.

Background-job worktree friction: the bg-isolation guard stops accepting Write/Edit to a freshly-created worktree mid-session once a prior worktree is pruned (binding doesn't follow). EnterWorktree errors for cwd-override sessions. The settings escape-hatch (worktree.bgIsolation:none) is correctly blocked by the auto-mode classifier as agent-config self-modification. Before implementing a fix for a GitHub issue, ALWAYS check for existing open PRs/branches already addressing it: 'gh pr list --search "<issue#>"' and 'git branch -a | grep <issue#>'. Missing this caused duplicate work on GH#330 — PR #362 (fix/deploy-invariant-330) already fixed it a day before #368 was built. The 'bd show'/'gh issue view' checks at session start are not enough; they don't reveal in-flight PRs.

CodeRabbit can emit a wrong 'Major' finding: on #310 it claimed the drift_ignore type enum was incomplete (missing 'stopped','extra') from a broad rg match; internal/reconcile/state.go:30-37 defines exactly 3 DriftType values (missing, image_mismatch, unhealthy). Always verify CodeRabbit's code claims against source before fixing.

CodeRabbit CHANGES_REQUESTED is a sticky reviewDecision: after you fix+push the requested change, the inline thread auto-resolves+outdates but the FORMAL review decision stays CHANGES_REQUESTED because CodeRabbit never dismisses its own review (and 'does not re-review already reviewed commits'). On bosun's UNPROTECTED main this is cosmetic — mergeStateStatus=UNSTABLE means mergeable-with-non-blocking-failing-check, NOT blocked. Exit the review loop on the 'does not re-review already reviewed commits' ack from a @coderabbitai re-trigger (coderabbit_incremental_silent) once all real CI is green + the thread is resolved/outdated; do NOT wait for the CHANGES_REQUESTED/CodeRabbit-check to flip green — it never will. (Contrast #368, which reached reviewDecision APPROVED because CodeRabbit had formally approved an earlier SHA first.)

CodeRabbit heading 'learnings' misfire on OpenSpec change files: it inconsistently demands '#' vs '##' first-line headings on proposal.md/tasks.md/design.md (wanted ## on #306 proposal, wanted '# Change:' H1 on #308/#310 tasks). These contradict openspec/AGENTS.md template AND all existing changes (7/9 tasks.md and 5/6 design.md start at ##, incl. merged #304/#306). Decline with that evidence; do not 'fix' — it creates inconsistency. Per Cameron's CLAUDE.md, evaluate CodeRabbit findings before adopting.

CodeRabbit misfire (PR #321, May 2026): flagged t.Fatal in a test as needing require.FailNow per 'project convention'. WRONG — repo uses t.Fatal/t.Fatalf 49x and require.FailNow 0x across internal/**/*_test.go. t.Fatal IS the convention. Decline with that census. Do NOT codify require.FailNow in language rules. Pattern: always verify CR 'convention' claims with a grep census before adopting (per Cameron CLAUDE.md CodeRabbit Feedback Loop).

Bosun README diagrams are generated from docs/diagrams/*.mmd by scripts/diagrams/render.mjs (beautiful-mermaid, make diagrams) into ASCII between <!-- DIAGRAM:id --> markers. Edit the .mmd source, never the README ASCII (clobbered on re-render). Width gotcha: box-drawing chars (┌─┐) are 3 bytes in UTF-8, so 'awk length' and 'wc -L' (non-UTF-8 locale) report ~3x the true visual width. Use python3 max(len(line)) for real column width. Fix for too-wide diagrams: flowchart LR -> TD (vertical). Shrank reconcile-pipeline from 251->65 cols this way (May 2026); added locking-singleflight.mmd.

The cadence git-safety hook (PreToolUse on Bash) HARD-BLOCKS compound git branch deletions — anything with a pipe, xargs, or '&&'-chained redirect (e.g. 'git branch --merged | grep | xargs git branch -d'). It only WARNS (allows) a plain single invocation. Workaround: delete merged branches with one multi-arg call: 'git branch -d a b c d' (still a single git command, no pipes). Hit during /outro cleanup May 2026. Applies to every cadence-hooked repo.

Two GitHub Actions facts (bosun PR #366, May 2026): (1) Posting a comment ON A PR via 'POST /issues/{n}/comments' (incl. actions/github-script github.rest.issues.createComment) requires BOTH 'issues: write' AND 'pull-requests: write' — issues:write alone 403s with 'Resource not accessible by integration'. The 'x-accepted-github-permissions: issues=write; pull_requests=write' response header is the authoritative tell (semicolon = all required). (2) For 'pull_request' events the workflow FILE is taken from the PR's HEAD ref, so committing a CI/workflow fix onto the feature branch self-heals THAT PR's own check on the next push — no separate PR needed. Corollary: an advisory/non-gating step (e.g. a nudge comment) must wrap its API mutations so a failure core.warning()s instead of failing the check.

OpenSpec validator gotcha: 'openspec validate <id> --strict' treats only the FIRST PHYSICAL LINE after '### Requirement: <name>' as the normative statement and requires SHALL/MUST on that line. Hard-wrapping the requirement body so SHALL lands on line 2 fails validation with 'must contain SHALL or MUST'. Keep the leading SHALL/MUST clause on line 1.

Bosun's reconcile state machine declared success BEFORE proving the operation — root class behind GH#330 and the May 2026 sweep (GH#331-361). Stages: (1) deploy invariant trusted WrittenFiles COUNT not on-disk truth (verify.go; fixed GH#330 content-equal check); (2) ComposeUpIsolated returned nil on PARTIAL failure (fixed GH#333 partialDeployError); (3) success-state SaveState runs before verifyPostDeploy so an unhealthy deploy is recorded as success, never retried (GH#336, still open). Hollow recovery — FIXED in PR #366: rollback expected loose files but Backup() writes configs.tar.gz, so extract-then-resolve (GH#332/#335); removeStaleFiles deleted live data, replaced by managed-set prune persisting state.deployed_files (GH#331). KEY for #331: bosun's /mnt/appdata is a BIND MOUNT of host /mnt/user/appdata — the SAME storage authelia/grafana/gatus write runtime data to (NOT a protective 'path split'), so the danger was real. Verify storage equivalence via bind mounts, not in-container paths — stat-ing the in-container alias on the host returns ENOENT, a false 'safe'. Gotcha: a dry-run still populates DeployResult.ManagedFiles (source walk runs regardless of DryRun), so guard state persistence with !DryRun. When touching reconcile success/state, verify on-disk/persisted truth, not counters/return-nil.

To cover createBackup's remote branch in reconcile tests without an SSH server: build a Reconciler with no TargetHost and pass nil secrets, so getTargetHost yields an unusable host that validateHost rejects. BackupRemote then fails fast at its validateHost guard (backup.go:202) before any ssh exec — covering the local=false branch (RemoteAppdataPath select + BackupRemote call + non-timeout error return) deterministically. See TestCreateBackup_RemotePathPropagatesFailure. Complements the chmod-0000 walk-error fault injection for backupFilesFromTargets.

Wedge-class bug sweep (May 2026, from #319): three recurring shapes in the long-running daemon — (1) recursive self-inclusion (tar archives its own output dir nested under a backed-up path: backup.go, fixed via #319/bosun-k88); (2) context-ignoring subprocess (exec.Command not CommandContext); (3) unbounded op with no size/time cap. #319 is the only CRITICAL reachable in default config. Deferred siblings filed as beads: bosun-9ep (reconcile decrypt/render/hooks have no per-step timeout — only git/compose/health do), bosun-kn1 (docker/client.go io.Copy/ReadAll ignore ctx; Ping shadows tighter caller deadline), bosun-7k3 (cmd webhook.go 5 handlers lack body cap that daemon/server.go has at 1MB — tunnel-exposed DoS; plus emergency.go runComposeUp had no ctx — bundled into bosun-k88; CLI subprocess gaps; .bak/CopyDir path-containment defensive).

When triaging a code-review finding, trace EVERY code path the finding could touch, not just the one matching its headline. On #375 (bosun-5qx), CodeRabbit's 'backupFilesFromTargets can return nil paths -> empty backup' finding matched the walk-error path (which DOES return partial paths -> I correctly judged handled), but that headline masked a SECOND path: discoverDeployTargets *failure* returns nil targets -> backupFilesFromTargets(nil) returns empty -> no-op backup. I initially skipped the finding on the first path's merits, then re-verified and found the valid second path. Lesson: a finding can be simultaneously wrong about path A and right about path B that share the same code. The 'verify each finding against current code' directive is precisely to catch this.
